title.en: Zeroes of a polynomial and their graphs
The curve that meets the road

text.en: A ball thrown upward follows a curve. The points where the curve touches the ground tell us when the ball is at height zero. Those points are the zeroes of a polynomial.

A polynomial of degree 1 is linear, of degree 2 is quadratic and of degree 3 is cubic. A quadratic looks like a x squared + b x + c with a not zero.
A zero of a polynomial p of x is a number k such that p of k equals 0.
Geometrically, the zeroes of p of x are the x-coordinates of the points where the graph of y = p of x meets the x-axis.
The graph of a linear polynomial is a straight line and it cuts the x-axis at exactly one point, so it has one zero.
The graph of a quadratic polynomial is a parabola. It opens upward if a is positive and downward if a is negative.
A parabola can cut the x-axis at two points, touch it at one point, or not meet it at all. So a quadratic has at most 2 zeroes.
A cubic polynomial has at most 3 zeroes because its graph can cross the x-axis at most three times.
For example, x squared - 3x - 4 = (x - 4)(x + 1), so its zeroes are 4 and minus 1 and the parabola cuts the x-axis there.

problem.en: Find the zeroes of x squared - 2x - 8.

why.en: Find two numbers with product -8 and sum -2: -4 and +2.

text.en: Put each factor equal to zero: x = 4 or x = -2.

why.en: A product is zero when a factor is zero.

text.en: So the parabola cuts the x-axis at (4, 0) and (-2, 0).

prompt.en: What do the zeroes of a polynomial mean on its graph?

requiredIdeas.en: Where the graph meets the x-axis
A quadratic has at most two

points.en: A zero of p(x) is a number k with p(k) = 0.
Zeroes are the x-coordinates of the points where y = p(x) cuts the x-axis.
A quadratic has at most 2 zeroes, a cubic at most 3.
The graph of a quadratic is a parabola.
